path.name: Your Creator Brand
path.tagline: Grow a personal brand on one platform and turn it into your first small brand deal or paid offer.
path.description: You decide who your content is for and what you want to be known for, then pick one platform and set up a clear profile. Over 30 days you study creators in your niche, plan two weeks of posts and publish consistently with just your phone and free tools. You practise hooks, reply to every comment, read your numbers and collaborate with peers. In the last week you build a simple media kit and UGC portfolio and pitch small brands honestly. Growth is usually slow at first, so the goal is a consistent posting habit, real feedback and your first professional brand pitches, not a follower number.
path.objective: Define your brand, set up one platform, post consistently from Day 4 or 5, build a media kit and UGC portfolio, send your first honest brand pitches and finish with real numbers and a plan for the next 30 days.
path.typicalPrice: Small brand deals and UGC gigs often start at $50–$300
firstTasks: Write who your content is for and what you want to be known for
Choose three content pillars and one main platform
Set up a clear bio, profile photo and link
Publish your first post by Day 4 or 5
workflow: Decide who your content is for and the one thing you want to be known for
Pick one main platform and set up a clear, honest profile
Study creators in your niche to learn formats, hooks and timing
Plan two weeks of posts around three content pillars
Post consistently and reply to every genuine comment
Read reach, saves, shares and follower growth, then adjust
Build a media kit and pitch small brands, always disclosing paid posts

tools.name: Your phone camera
tools.purpose: Film and photograph all of your content; natural window light is enough

tools.name: CapCut
tools.purpose: Edit short videos, add captions and trim to the best moments

tools.name: Canva
tools.purpose: Design carousels, covers, your media kit and your UGC portfolio

tools.name: Platform analytics
tools.purpose: Read reach, saves, shares and follower growth inside your chosen app

tools.name: Google Sheets
tools.purpose: Keep your content calendar, weekly numbers and brand list in one place

tools.name: Link-in-bio page
tools.purpose: Pick one, such as Linktree, Beacons or Stan, to hold your links and media kit

plan.missionTitle: Decide who your content is for and what you want to be known for.
plan.goal: Write a one-sentence brand statement and your 30-day goal.

tasks.title: Watch the Day 1 lesson
tasks.description: See how a personal brand works: one audience, one clear topic and a reason to follow you instead of anyone else.

tasks.title: Name your audience
tasks.description: Write who you want to reach in plain words. Be specific enough that one person could read it and think "that is me".

tasks.title: List what you know
tasks.description: Write ten things you know, are learning or do every week that this audience would find useful or interesting.

tasks.title: Write your brand statement
tasks.description: Use this shape: "I help [audience] with [topic] by sharing [what you post]." Keep it to one sentence.

tasks.title: Set your 30-day goal
tasks.description: Choose a goal you control, such as "post 3 times a week and send 5 brand pitches". Followers and income are not fully in your control yet.

plan.nicheHint: Start from this draft: I help {audience} with {problem} in {niche}. Then circle the one thing from your list you could talk about every week for a year.

stageHints.idea: Pick the audience you understand best, ideally one you belong to or used to belong to.
stageHints.started: Look at your past posts and write the statement they were really trying to say.
stageHints.some_traction: Write the statement around the posts your followers already save and share most.
stageHints.already_earning: Write down what brands or buyers paid you for; this month builds your brand around that.

plan.missionTitle: Choose three content pillars your brand will be known for.
plan.goal: Write three pillars with five post ideas each.

tasks.title: Watch the Day 2 lesson
tasks.description: Learn how content pillars keep you consistent without running out of ideas, and why three is enough to start.

tasks.title: Pick three pillars
tasks.description: Choose three topics that fit your brand statement, such as one teaching pillar, one personal pillar and one behind-the-scenes pillar.

tasks.title: Fill each pillar
tasks.description: Write five post ideas under each pillar. Short, rough titles are fine.

tasks.title: Check the fit
tasks.description: For each idea ask: would my audience save, share or comment on this? Cross out anything that is only for you.

tasks.title: Note what you will not post
tasks.description: Write two topics you will keep off your brand, such as your home location or your family's private life.

plan.nicheHint: Try these pillars as a start: tips about {problem}, your own journey in {niche}, and answers to questions {audience} ask. Adjust the wording until it sounds like you.

stageHints.idea: Pick pillars you can talk about without notes; you can refine them after your first posts.
stageHints.started: Sort your existing posts into three groups and name the pillars from what you see.
stageHints.some_traction: Keep the pillar that performs best and test whether the other two still earn their place.
stageHints.already_earning: Make sure one pillar shows the kind of work brands or buyers have paid you for.

plan.missionTitle: Choose one main platform to grow on this month.
plan.goal: Pick your main platform and write why it fits.

tasks.title: Watch the Day 3 lesson
tasks.description: Compare Instagram, TikTok, LinkedIn, X and YouTube Shorts in plain terms, and why one platform done well beats five done badly.

tasks.title: Find your audience
tasks.description: Search your topic on two or three platforms and note where your audience's conversations are most active.

tasks.title: Match your strengths
tasks.description: Note whether you prefer talking on camera, writing or showing visuals. Pick the platform that rewards what you enjoy.

tasks.title: Choose one
tasks.description: Write your main platform and one sentence on why. Other platforms can wait until your habit is steady.

tasks.title: Secure your name
tasks.description: Check that your preferred handle is available. Keep it simple, easy to spell and free of personal details.

plan.nicheHint: Search for {terms} on two platforms and note where {audience} ask the most questions about {problem}. That is usually your best first platform.

stageHints.idea: Pick the app you already open daily; you understand its style without studying it.
stageHints.started: Stay on the platform where you already post unless your audience is clearly elsewhere.
stageHints.some_traction: Keep your growing platform as the main one; do not split your energy this month.
stageHints.already_earning: Choose the platform where brands in your niche are already working with creators.

plan.missionTitle: Set up a clear profile and publish your first post.
plan.goal: Finish your bio, photo and link, then publish an intro post.

tasks.title: Watch the Day 4 lesson
tasks.description: See what a clear profile does in the first three seconds: who you help, what you post and what to do next.

tasks.title: Write your bio
tasks.description: Turn your brand statement into a short bio: who it is for, what they get, and one line of proof or personality.

tasks.title: Choose a profile photo
tasks.description: Use a clear, well-lit photo of your face or a simple logo. Avoid photos that show your home, street or school.

tasks.title: Add one link
tasks.description: Add a link-in-bio page with a short welcome and, later, your media kit. One link is enough for now.

tasks.title: Publish an intro post
tasks.description: Post a short intro: who you are, who this account is for and what you will share. Done is better than perfect.

plan.nicheHint: Write a bio line in this shape: Helping {audience} with {problem}. Then read it aloud and cut any word that does not help a stranger decide to follow.

stageHints.idea: Your first post can be simple: say hello and what you will share. Nobody expects a polished start.
stageHints.started: Update your bio to match your brand statement before you post again.
stageHints.some_traction: Refresh your bio and pinned posts so new visitors see your best work first.
stageHints.already_earning: Add a line or link showing you are open to brand partnerships.

plan.missionTitle: Study ten creators in your niche to learn what works.
plan.goal: Fill in notes on 10 creators and publish your second post.

tasks.title: Watch the Day 5 lesson
tasks.description: Learn how to study creators without copying them: formats, hooks, lengths and posting times.

tasks.title: Find ten creators
tasks.description: Pick ten creators in your niche, ideally a mix of small and medium accounts close to where you are.

tasks.title: Note formats and hooks
tasks.description: For each one note their best-performing format, the first line of three top posts and roughly when they post.

tasks.title: Spot the gaps
tasks.description: Write three things your audience asks about that these creators rarely cover or explain simply.

tasks.title: Publish your second post
tasks.description: Post one idea from your pillars, borrowing a format you saw but using your own words, story and examples.

plan.nicheHint: Search for {terms} and note how {audience} describe {problem} in comments. Their exact words make strong hooks later.

stageHints.idea: Study accounts only a little ahead of you; their steps are easier to follow than huge creators'.
stageHints.started: Compare your recent posts with the creators you studied and note one format to try.
stageHints.some_traction: Look for creators at your size to collaborate with in Week 3.
stageHints.already_earning: Note which creators in your niche work with brands and how they disclose those posts.

plan.missionTitle: Plan two weeks of content around your pillars.
plan.goal: Fill in a 2-week content calendar.

tasks.title: Watch the Day 6 lesson
tasks.description: See how a simple calendar removes the daily "what do I post" stress and keeps your pillars balanced.

tasks.title: Choose your rhythm
tasks.description: Pick a posting rhythm you can keep, such as three or four posts a week. Consistent beats frequent.

tasks.title: Fill the calendar
tasks.description: Place your pillar ideas on specific days for the next two weeks, rotating between pillars.

tasks.title: Pick posting times
tasks.description: Use the times you noted from other creators as a starting point; your own analytics will refine them later.

tasks.title: Prepare one post now
tasks.description: Write the hook and outline for your next post so tomorrow starts easy.

plan.nicheHint: Make sure at least half of your planned posts answer a real question {audience} have about {problem}.

stageHints.idea: Plan only what you can keep up; three posts a week is a strong start.
stageHints.started: Plan around the days you actually managed to post in the past.
stageHints.some_traction: Plan more of the pillar your analytics show is working.
stageHints.already_earning: Leave room in the calendar for brand content later, clearly marked.

plan.missionTitle: Learn to write hooks that earn the first three seconds.
plan.goal: Write 10 hooks for your planned posts.

tasks.title: Watch the Day 7 lesson
tasks.description: Learn the main hook types: question, bold statement, mistake, result and story, and how to keep them honest.

tasks.title: Read the hook bank
tasks.description: Go through the hook bank and mark the five styles that fit your voice.

tasks.title: Write ten hooks
tasks.description: Write one hook for each of your next ten planned posts.

tasks.title: Cut clickbait
tasks.description: Remove any hook that promises something the post does not deliver. Honest hooks build trust.

tasks.title: Post with your best hook
tasks.description: Publish your next post using the strongest hook and note it in your calendar.

plan.nicheHint: Try this hook: The mistake most {audience} make with {problem}. Then make sure the post actually explains that mistake and the fix.

stageHints.idea: Your hooks will feel awkward at first; writing ten makes the eleventh easier.
stageHints.started: Rewrite the first line of your three most recent posts and compare.
stageHints.some_traction: Look at your top three posts and note which hook type they used.
stageHints.already_earning: Practise hooks that work for brand content too, such as a problem the product solves.

plan.missionTitle: Batch-create several posts with only your phone and free tools.
plan.goal: Film or design three posts in one session.

tasks.title: Watch the Day 8 lesson
tasks.description: See a simple phone setup: window light, steady phone, clear sound and free editing in CapCut or Canva.

tasks.title: Set up your space
tasks.description: Find a spot with soft window light and a tidy background. Check nothing personal, like your address, is visible.

tasks.title: Batch three posts
tasks.description: Film or design three posts from your calendar in one session.

tasks.title: Edit simply
tasks.description: Trim slow starts, add captions and keep only what helps the viewer.

tasks.title: Schedule or save
tasks.description: Save the posts as drafts or schedule them for the days in your calendar.

plan.nicheHint: Pick three ideas about {problem} that you can show, not just tell, such as a quick before and after for {audience}.

stageHints.idea: Your first edits do not need effects; clear captions and a fast start matter most.
stageHints.started: Batching saves time; try filming three posts in the time one usually takes.
stageHints.some_traction: Batch a full week so you can spend more time engaging with your audience.
stageHints.already_earning: Batch your regular content so you have time for brand projects.

plan.missionTitle: Use simple storytelling to make your posts memorable.
plan.goal: Publish one story-based post.

tasks.title: Watch the Day 9 lesson
tasks.description: Learn a simple story shape: situation, problem, turning point, lesson. It works in 30 seconds or a short caption.

tasks.title: Pick a real moment
tasks.description: Choose a real moment from your journey that relates to one of your pillars.

tasks.title: Shape it
tasks.description: Write it as situation, problem, turning point and lesson in under 100 words.

tasks.title: Protect privacy
tasks.description: Remove names, places and details about other people, especially children, unless they have agreed.

tasks.title: Publish it
tasks.description: Post the story with a hook from your list and ask one simple question at the end.

plan.nicheHint: Tell a short story about a time you or someone like {audience} struggled with {problem} and what changed.

stageHints.idea: A small everyday story is enough; you do not need a dramatic one.
stageHints.started: Turn one of your past tips into a story about how you learned it.
stageHints.some_traction: Share a story behind one of your best-performing posts.
stageHints.already_earning: Share a story about a result you helped someone get, with their permission.

plan.missionTitle: Repurpose one idea into several formats.
plan.goal: Turn one post into three formats.

tasks.title: Watch the Day 10 lesson
tasks.description: See how one strong idea can become a video, a carousel, a text post and a story without extra research.

tasks.title: Pick your best idea
tasks.description: Choose the post or idea that got the best reaction so far.

tasks.title: Follow the checklist
tasks.description: Use the repurposing checklist to plan three versions of it.

tasks.title: Create two new versions
tasks.description: Make two of the formats with CapCut or Canva.

tasks.title: Add them to the calendar
tasks.description: Place the new versions in your calendar a few days apart.

plan.nicheHint: Take your clearest tip about {problem} and turn it into a short video, a carousel and a text post for {audience}.

stageHints.idea: Repurposing is not cheating; most people miss most of your posts.
stageHints.started: Repurpose an older post that deserved more views.
stageHints.some_traction: Repurpose your top post into a format you have not tried yet.
stageHints.already_earning: Repurposing also shows brands you can create in several formats.

plan.missionTitle: Practise showing up on camera, or choose a faceless style that suits you.
plan.goal: Record and publish one short talking or voiceover video.

tasks.title: Watch the Day 11 lesson
tasks.description: Learn simple ways to feel calmer on camera, and how faceless options like voiceover, hands-only or screen recordings can work too.

tasks.title: Choose your style
tasks.description: Decide between face, voiceover, hands-only or screen recording. Any of them can build a brand.

tasks.title: Practise three takes
tasks.description: Record the same 20-second tip three times. Keep the best one; delete the rest.

tasks.title: Use notes
tasks.description: Write three bullet points to glance at instead of a full script.

tasks.title: Publish it
tasks.description: Post the best take with captions. Notice that the second video is easier than the first.

plan.nicheHint: Record one 20-second tip about {problem} for {audience}, using three bullet points as your only notes.

stageHints.idea: Start with voiceover or hands-only if showing your face feels like too much.
stageHints.started: Try one format you have avoided and compare how it performs.
stageHints.some_traction: Test talking directly to camera if you have mostly used text or voiceover.
stageHints.already_earning: Short, clear talking videos are what many brands ask for in UGC.

plan.missionTitle: Write captions that add value and ask for one clear action.
plan.goal: Add clear captions and calls to action to three posts.

tasks.title: Watch the Day 12 lesson
tasks.description: Learn how captions, on-screen text and a single call to action help people save, share and follow.

tasks.title: Add on-screen text
tasks.description: Make sure your key point is readable without sound.

tasks.title: Write a useful caption
tasks.description: Add one extra tip or detail in the caption, not just hashtags.

tasks.title: Choose one call to action
tasks.description: Ask for one thing: save, share, comment or follow. One ask works better than four.

tasks.title: Use a few relevant tags
tasks.description: Add a small number of hashtags or keywords that describe the post, not trending ones that do not fit.

plan.nicheHint: End your next post with: Save this if you are working on {problem}. Then check that the post is worth saving.

stageHints.idea: Use the same simple call to action for a week so it becomes a habit.
stageHints.started: Add a clear call to action to your next three posts and compare comments.
stageHints.some_traction: Test which call to action brings the most saves or follows.
stageHints.already_earning: Practise calls to action you could also use in brand content.

plan.missionTitle: Protect your privacy and the people around you.
plan.goal: Run a privacy check on your profile and posts.

tasks.title: Watch the Day 13 lesson
tasks.description: Learn what to keep off camera: your address, school, routine, number plates and details about children and family.

tasks.title: Check your profile
tasks.description: Remove anything that reveals your home location, workplace or daily routine.

tasks.title: Review your posts
tasks.description: Look at every post for street names, house numbers, mail, school logos or tagged locations.

tasks.title: Set family rules
tasks.description: Decide what you will and will not share about children and family. Ask adults before you feature them.

tasks.title: Tighten settings
tasks.description: Review comment filters and who can message you in your app's privacy settings.

plan.nicheHint: Plan how to talk about {problem} using your experience without sharing private details about where you live or who you live with.

stageHints.idea: Start private-by-default; it is easier to share more later than to take things back.
stageHints.started: Delete or edit any older post that shows where you live.
stageHints.some_traction: As you grow, review tagged locations and comments more often.
stageHints.already_earning: Use a separate business email for brand conversations.

plan.missionTitle: Review two weeks of posting and adjust your plan.
plan.goal: Write your numbers and plan the next two weeks.

tasks.title: Watch the Day 14 lesson
tasks.description: Look back at your first posts without judging them, and decide what to keep, change or drop.

tasks.title: Count your posts
tasks.description: Write how many posts you published and how many you planned.

tasks.title: Note early signals
tasks.description: For each post note reach, saves, shares and comments. Early numbers are small; look for patterns, not totals.

tasks.title: Pick one change
tasks.description: Choose one thing to change, such as hook style, posting time or format.

tasks.title: Plan the next two weeks
tasks.description: Fill the next two weeks of your calendar with that change built in.

plan.nicheHint: Note which post about {problem} got the most saves or comments from {audience}, and plan two more like it.

stageHints.idea: If you posted at all this week, you are ahead of most people who only plan.
stageHints.started: Compare your posting rhythm now with before this month.
stageHints.some_traction: Write which pillar is growing fastest and give it more space.
stageHints.already_earning: Note which posts would make good examples in your media kit.

plan.missionTitle: Build community by replying thoughtfully to your comments.
plan.goal: Reply to every genuine comment and start three conversations.

tasks.title: Watch the Day 15 lesson
tasks.description: Learn why replies matter: comments are conversations, and the people who comment are your future community.

tasks.title: Reply to every comment
tasks.description: Reply to each genuine comment on your last five posts with more than an emoji or a single word.

tasks.title: Ask a follow-up question
tasks.description: Turn three replies into conversations by asking something specific.

tasks.title: Note recurring questions
tasks.description: Write down questions people ask; they are your next post ideas.

tasks.title: Thank new followers
tasks.description: Where it feels natural, thank new followers who engaged, without sending sales messages.

plan.nicheHint: Write down every question {audience} asked you about {problem}. Each one can become a post.

stageHints.idea: Even one comment deserves a thoughtful reply; it shows new visitors you are listening.
stageHints.started: Go back to older posts and reply to any comments you missed.
stageHints.some_traction: Set a daily time to reply so engagement does not take over your day.
stageHints.already_earning: Keep replying personally even as your audience grows; brands notice real community.

plan.missionTitle: Engage genuinely with other creators in your niche.
plan.goal: Leave ten thoughtful comments on peers' posts.

tasks.title: Watch the Day 16 lesson
tasks.description: Learn how genuine comments build relationships and visibility, and why to avoid follow-for-follow and engagement pods, which hurt your account and trust.

tasks.title: Pick ten peers
tasks.description: Choose ten creators near your size in your niche.

tasks.title: Leave real comments
tasks.description: Write ten comments that add something: a question, an example or a specific compliment.

tasks.title: Skip shortcuts
tasks.description: Do not join engagement pods or follow-for-follow groups, and never buy followers or likes. They give fake numbers brands can spot.

tasks.title: Save your list
tasks.description: Keep your peer list; you will use it for collaborations on Day 19.

plan.nicheHint: Find ten creators who also talk to {audience} about {problem} and comment on one post each with a real thought.

stageHints.idea: You do not need followers to comment; your comments are often how the first ones find you.
stageHints.started: Comment consistently on the same peers for a week to build real relationships.
stageHints.some_traction: Engage with creators slightly bigger than you; thoughtful comments get noticed.
stageHints.already_earning: Comment on brand accounts in your niche too, genuinely, before you pitch them.

plan.missionTitle: Learn to read reach, saves, shares and follower growth.
plan.goal: Fill in your analytics review.

tasks.title: Watch the Day 17 lesson
tasks.description: Learn what each number means: reach shows how far a post went, saves and shares show value, follower growth shows trust.

tasks.title: Open your analytics
tasks.description: Switch to a creator or professional account if needed; it is free on most platforms and unlocks basic numbers.

tasks.title: Fill the guide
tasks.description: Record reach, saves, shares, comments and follows for your last ten posts.

tasks.title: Find your top three
tasks.description: Mark your three best posts and write what they have in common.

tasks.title: Write one insight
tasks.description: Write one sentence: "My audience responds most to...".

plan.nicheHint: Look at which posts about {problem} reached the most {audience} and note the hook, format and posting time.

stageHints.idea: Small numbers are normal now; you are looking for what works relatively better.
stageHints.started: Compare your first week with your second and note what improved.
stageHints.some_traction: Track your engagement trend over four weeks, not single posts.
stageHints.already_earning: Save your best numbers; brands will ask for them in your media kit.

plan.missionTitle: Make more of what your audience responds to.
plan.goal: Plan and create three posts based on your best performer.

tasks.title: Watch the Day 18 lesson
tasks.description: See how to turn one good post into a series without repeating yourself.

tasks.title: Choose your best post
tasks.description: Pick the post with the most saves or shares from your analytics review.

tasks.title: Plan a series
tasks.description: Write three follow-up ideas: a part two, a deeper example and an answer to a comment.

tasks.title: Create them
tasks.description: Make the three posts using the same format and a fresh hook for each.

tasks.title: Update the calendar
tasks.description: Add them to your calendar over the next week.

plan.nicheHint: Turn your best post about {problem} into a three-part series for {audience}.

stageHints.idea: If no post stands out yet, repeat your favourite format three times and compare.
stageHints.started: Make a part two of your best recent post.
stageHints.some_traction: Turn your top topic into a recurring weekly series.
stageHints.already_earning: A recurring series is easy for brands to imagine joining.

plan.missionTitle: Find peers to collaborate with.
plan.goal: Send three friendly collaboration ideas to peers.

tasks.title: Watch the Day 19 lesson
tasks.description: Learn simple collaboration formats: duets or stitches, joint lives, guest posts, shared carousels and swap features.

tasks.title: Pick three peers
tasks.description: Choose three creators from your peer list who share your audience but not your exact topic.

tasks.title: Suggest one idea
tasks.description: For each, write one specific idea that helps both audiences.

tasks.title: Send a friendly message
tasks.description: Send a short, friendly message with the idea. Keep it personal; mention a post of theirs you liked.

tasks.title: Track replies
tasks.description: Note who replied and plan follow-ups politely after a few days.

plan.nicheHint: Look for creators who reach {audience} from a different angle, so a collaboration about {problem} adds value to both.

stageHints.idea: Collaborating early is normal; peers at your stage are often happy to try.
stageHints.started: Collaborate with someone you have already exchanged comments with.
stageHints.some_traction: Suggest a recurring collaboration with your strongest peer.
stageHints.already_earning: Collaborations also give you new examples for your media kit.

plan.missionTitle: Create and publish one collaboration post.
plan.goal: Publish one collaboration or response post.

tasks.title: Watch the Day 20 lesson
tasks.description: See how to plan a collaboration so both creators look good and the audience gets value.

tasks.title: Agree the plan
tasks.description: Agree the topic, format, posting date and who posts what.

tasks.title: Create your part
tasks.description: Film or design your part with a clear hook and both names visible.

tasks.title: Publish and tag
tasks.description: Publish and tag your partner using the platform's collaboration feature if available.

tasks.title: If no one replied yet
tasks.description: Make a response or duet post to a peer's public video, with credit, as your collaboration for today.

plan.nicheHint: Collaborate on a post that answers one question {audience} ask about {problem}, with each of you sharing a different view.

stageHints.idea: A simple duet or response post with credit counts as your first collaboration.
stageHints.started: Pick a partner whose audience is close to yours in size.
stageHints.some_traction: Measure what the collaboration brought: reach, follows and comments.
stageHints.already_earning: Practise agreeing scope and dates; it is the same skill you need for brand deals.

plan.missionTitle: Set boundaries for comments and protect your energy.
plan.goal: Write your comment policy and response plan.

tasks.title: Watch the Day 21 lesson
tasks.description: Learn to tell honest criticism from trolling, when to reply, when to ignore and when to block or report.

tasks.title: Sort the comment
tasks.description: Write three categories: useful criticism, misunderstanding and abuse.

tasks.title: Write your replies
tasks.description: Write a calm reply template for useful criticism and for misunderstandings.

tasks.title: Set filters
tasks.description: Add hidden-word filters for abuse and decide when you block or report.

tasks.title: Plan your recovery
tasks.description: Write one thing you will do when a comment stings, such as stepping away for an hour before replying.

plan.nicheHint: Prepare a calm reply for the most common pushback {audience} might give about how you talk about {problem}.

stageHints.idea: Most early comments are kind; prepare now so the first unkind one does not stop you.
stageHints.started: Review any past negative comment and write how you would answer it now.
stageHints.some_traction: As reach grows, use filters and blocking without guilt.
stageHints.already_earning: Brands value creators who handle comments calmly in public.

plan.missionTitle: Create a simple one-page media kit.
plan.goal: Finish a one-page media kit.

tasks.title: Watch the Day 22 lesson
tasks.description: See what brands look for in a media kit: who you reach, what you create, honest numbers and how to contact you.

tasks.title: Use the template
tasks.description: Open the media kit template in Canva or Google Slides.

tasks.title: Add your story
tasks.description: Write a short intro: who you are, who your audience is and what you post.

tasks.title: Add honest numbers
tasks.description: Add followers, average reach and engagement from your analytics. Never round up or invent numbers.

tasks.title: Add examples
tasks.description: Add three of your best posts and a professional contact email.

plan.nicheHint: Describe your audience as specifically as you can, such as {audience} interested in {problem}, so brands in {niche} see the fit.

stageHints.idea: A small, honest kit is fine; brands working with small creators care about fit more than size.
stageHints.started: Highlight your consistency and your most engaged posts.
stageHints.some_traction: Show your growth trend from this month as well as totals.
stageHints.already_earning: Add past partnerships and results, with permission from those brands.

plan.missionTitle: Create two sample UGC videos for your portfolio.
plan.goal: Publish a simple UGC portfolio with two samples.

tasks.title: Watch the Day 23 lesson
tasks.description: Learn what UGC is: brands pay creators for content the brand posts itself, so your follower count matters less than your filming skills.

tasks.title: Read the checklist
tasks.description: Go through the UGC portfolio checklist.

tasks.title: Pick two products you own
tasks.description: Choose two products you already own and genuinely use. Do not tag brands or imply a partnership.

tasks.title: Film two samples
tasks.description: Film two short samples: one unboxing or first impression and one problem and solution video.

tasks.title: Collect them

plan.nicheHint: Film samples with products {audience} would use for {problem}, so your portfolio fits brands in {niche}.

stageHints.idea: UGC is a good first income path because brands judge your videos, not your follower count.

plan.missionTitle: Build a list of small brands that fit your niche.

tasks.title: Watch the Day 24 lesson
tasks.description: Learn where to find small brands that work with creators and how to check they fit your audience and values.

tasks.title: Start with what you use

tasks.title: Search small brands

tasks.title: Find the right contact

tasks.title: Check the fit
tasks.description: Keep only brands you would genuinely recommend. Skip anything you would not use yourself.

plan.nicheHint: Search for {terms} plus words like "small business" or "handmade" to find brands that sell to {audience}.

stageHints.idea: Start with brands you already use; your honest experience makes your pitch stronger.

stageHints.already_earning: Revisit brands you worked with and ask about repeat projects.

plan.missionTitle: Decide how to price your first brand deal or UGC gig.

tasks.title: Watch the Day 25 lesson
tasks.description: Learn what affects a price: deliverables, usage rights, time, exclusivity and your audience, and why beginner rates are a start, not your worth.

tasks.title: List deliverables

resources.title: Brand Statement Worksheet
resources.description: Define who your content is for and what you want to be known for. Fill it in on Days 1 and 4.

sections.heading: Your audience
body: Write who you want to reach in one sentence.
Note what they struggle with or care about.
Note where they spend time online.

sections.heading: What you know
body: List ten things you know or are learning.
Circle the three your audience would value most.
Note which ones you could talk about every week.

sections.heading: Your statement
body: I help [audience] with [topic] by sharing [what you post].
Read it aloud and cut extra words.
Ask: would a stranger know if this is for them?

sections.heading: Your bio
body: Line 1: who it is for and what they get.
Line 2: one line of proof or personality.
Line 3: what to do next, such as follow or tap the link.

resources.title: Content Pillars Planner
resources.description: Plan three content pillars with five post ideas each. Use it on Day 2 and whenever ideas run low.

sections.heading: Pillar 1: Teach
body: Name the pillar.
Write five tips, how-tos or mistakes to avoid.
Mark the one you can post first.

sections.heading: Pillar 2: Personal
body: Name the pillar.
Write five stories, opinions or lessons from your journey.
Check none reveal private details.

sections.heading: Pillar 3: Behind the scenes
body: Name the pillar.
Write five ideas showing your process, tools or routine.
Keep your home location and family out of frame.

sections.heading: Off-limits list
body: Write topics you will not post about.
Include your address, school or workplace and children's details.
Review this list every month.

resources.title: Hook Bank
resources.description: Fill-in-the-blank hooks for your first lines. Always deliver what the hook promises.

sections.heading: Question hooks
body: Are you still [common mistake]?
What would you do if [situation]?
Why does [problem] keep happening?

sections.heading: Statement hooks
body: The easiest way to [result] I have found.
Stop [habit] if you want [result].
Nobody told me this about [topic].

sections.heading: Story hooks
body: A year ago I [situation].
This happened when I tried [thing].
The moment I realised [lesson].

sections.heading: Honesty check
body: Does the post deliver what the hook promises?
Did you avoid exaggerating results?
Would you be happy if a friend read it?

resources.title: 2-Week Content Calendar
resources.description: Plan two weeks of posts around your pillars. Use it on Day 6 and refresh it every two weeks.

sections.heading: Rhythm
body: Choose how many posts per week you can keep.
Pick your posting days.
Pick a starting posting time for each day.

sections.heading: Week A
body: Write the pillar, idea and format for each posting day.
Add a hook from the hook bank.
Mark which posts are batched and ready.

sections.heading: Week B
body: Repeat the same layout for the second week.
Rotate pillars so no pillar appears twice in a row.
Leave one slot for a reply-to-comment post.

sections.heading: Review
body: After two weeks, mark posted or missed.
Note your top post.
Carry one learning into the next calendar.

resources.title: Repurposing Checklist
resources.description: Turn one idea into several formats without extra research.

sections.heading: Pick the idea
body: It got good saves, shares or comments.
It answers a real audience question.
It can be explained in several ways.

sections.heading: Formats
body: Short video with captions.
Carousel with one point per slide.
Text post or thread.
Story with a poll or question.

sections.heading: Adapt
body: Write a fresh hook for each format.
Resize designs for each placement in Canva.
Keep the core message the same.

sections.heading: Schedule
body: Space versions a few days apart.
Add them to your calendar.
Compare how each format performs.

resources.title: Analytics Review Guide
resources.description: Read your numbers calmly and find what to do more of. Use it on Days 14, 17 and 30.

sections.heading: What each number means
body: Reach: how many accounts saw the post.
Saves and shares: how useful or relatable it was.
Follows from the post: how much it built trust.

sections.heading: Track ten posts
body: Write reach, saves, shares, comments and follows for each.
Note hook type, format and posting time.
Mark your top three.

sections.heading: Find patterns
body: What do your top three have in common?
What do your lowest three have in common?
Write one sentence: my audience responds most to...

sections.heading: Decide
body: Pick one thing to do more of.
Pick one thing to change or drop.
Check again in two weeks.

resources.title: Media Kit Template
resources.description: A one-page media kit you can build in Canva or Google Slides. Use it on Day 22.

sections.heading: About you
body: Your name or handle and photo.
One sentence on who your content is for.
Your three content pillars.

sections.heading: Audience and numbers
body: Followers on your main platform.
Average reach and engagement from your analytics.
Audience details you can see, such as top locations and age range. Never invent or round up.

sections.heading: Work examples
body: Three of your best posts with links.
Two UGC samples.
Any past partnerships, with permission.

sections.heading: Contact
body: A professional email address.
What you offer, such as posts, UGC videos or stories.
Rates on request, or your starting rates.

resources.title: UGC Portfolio Checklist
resources.description: Make a simple portfolio that shows brands what you can film. Use it on Day 23.

sections.heading: Samples
body: Two to four short videos.
Products you own and genuinely use.
No brand tags or anything that implies a partnership.

sections.heading: Styles
body: Unboxing or first impression.
Problem and solution.
Tutorial or how-to.
Simple testimonial in your own words.

sections.heading: Quality
body: Good natural light and clear sound.
Hook in the first two seconds.
Captions and a clean ending.

sections.heading: Presentation
body: Collect samples in a Canva page or shared folder.
Add a one-line intro and contact email.
Link it from your media kit and bio page.

resources.title: Brand Pitch Template
resources.description: A short, honest email to pitch a brand. Personalise every pitch. Use it on Days 25 and 27.

sections.heading: Subject line
body: Content idea for [brand] from a [niche] creator
Keep it clear and specific.
Avoid hype or urgency.

sections.heading: Opening
body: Hi [name], I am [name], I create content about [topic] for [audience].
Mention how you already use or like their product.
Keep it to two sentences.

sections.heading: Your idea
body: Suggest one content idea that fits the product and your audience.
Mention the format, such as one short video or a UGC video for their ads.
Say that any paid post will be clearly disclosed.

sections.heading: Close
body: Link your media kit and UGC portfolio.
Offer starting rates or invite them to share their budget.
Thank them and sign off with your contact details.

resources.title: Paid-Post Disclosure Checklist
resources.description: Disclose paid, gifted and affiliate content clearly every time. Use it on Day 26 and before every brand post.

sections.heading: When to disclose
body: You were paid in money.
You received a free product or service.
You use an affiliate link or code.
You have a personal connection to the brand.

sections.heading: How to disclose
body: Put #ad or "Paid partnership with [brand]" at the start of the caption.
Turn on the platform's paid partnership or branded-content tool.
Say it out loud in videos where possible.

sections.heading: What not to do
body: Do not hide the label among hashtags.
Do not use vague labels like #sp or #collab alone.
Do not agree to any request to hide that a post is paid.

sections.heading: Before posting
body: Check the brand's brief matches what you agreed.
Check claims are honest and not medical or financial promises.
Check your disclosure is visible without tapping more.

text.creator_brand:
The easiest posts answer questions your audience already asks.

1. Open your content pillars and pick the one you have posted least.
2. Read comments on your posts and on peers' posts in your niche, and copy three real questions.
3. Answer one question in a short post with a clear hook.

Next step: write three post ideas from real questions and add them to your calendar.

followUps: How do I write a better hook?

text.creator_brand:
Low reach is common in the first months, and nobody can promise how an algorithm will treat a post. What you control is whether people stay, save and share.

1. Check your last ten posts and find the two with the best reach.
2. Compare their hooks, formats and posting times with your weakest posts.
3. Make your next post in the style of your best one, with a stronger first line.

Next step: rewrite the hook of your next planned post three ways and use the clearest one.

followUps: How do I read my analytics?
How do I write a better hook?

text.creator_brand:
Every account starts at zero, and growth is usually slow at first. Avoid shortcuts: never buy followers or join follow-for-follow groups, because fake numbers hurt your reach and brands can spot them.

1. Make sure your bio says who you help and what they get.
2. Post consistently for four weeks around your three pillars.
3. Leave ten thoughtful comments a day on peers' posts in your niche.

Next step: rewrite your bio so a stranger knows in three seconds if your account is for them.

followUps: How do I engage without being spammy?
Can I earn with a small audience?

text.creator_brand:
A hook earns the first two or three seconds; the rest of the post has to keep its promise.

1. Open the hook bank and pick a question, statement or story hook.
2. Write three versions for your next post.
3. Read them aloud and keep the one that is clearest and honest.

Next step: write ten hooks for your next ten posts in one sitting.

followUps: How do I tell a short story?

text.creator_brand:
Consistent beats frequent. Three posts a week you can keep up beat daily posts for a week and then silence.

1. Choose a rhythm you can keep even in a busy week.
2. Fill a 2-week content calendar.
3. Batch-create three posts in one session.

Next step: block one hour this week to batch your next three posts.

Almost everyone feels awkward on camera at first. It gets easier with practice, and faceless styles can build a brand too.

1. Choose a style: face, voiceover, hands-only or screen recording.
2. Write three bullet points instead of a script.
3. Record the same 20-second tip three times and keep the best.

Next step: record one short take today; you do not have to post it yet.

Can faceless accounts get brand deals?

text.creator_brand:
Pick one main platform this month. One platform done well beats five done badly.

1. Search your topic on two or three platforms and see where your audience asks questions.
2. Match the platform to what you enjoy: talking on camera, writing or visuals.
3. Choose one and post there consistently for 30 days.

Next step: write your main platform and one sentence on why it fits.

text.creator_brand:
Small brands often work with small creators when the fit is clear. Nobody can guarantee a deal, but a professional, honest pitch gives you a real chance.

1. Build a one-page media kit with honest numbers.
2. List 15 small brands you genuinely use or would recommend.
3. Send five short, personalised pitches with one content idea each.

Next step: open the brand pitch template and personalise it for your top brand.

followUps: Do I have to say a post is paid?

text.creator_brand:
Price your time first, then adjust for usage rights and your audience. Beginner rates are a starting point, not your worth.

1. List what the brand wants: posts, videos, stories and how long they can use them.
2. Estimate your hours for planning, filming, editing and changes.
3. Set a price that covers your time, and add a separate price for extra usage rights.

Next step: write starting rates for one post, one UGC video and one story set.

followUps: Should I work for free products?

text.creator_brand:
UGC means brands pay you to create videos they post on their own accounts or ads. Your filming skills matter more than your follower count, which makes it a good first path.

1. Pick two products you own and genuinely use.
2. Film one first-impression video and one problem-and-solution video.
3. Put them on a simple Canva page and link it from your media kit.

Next step: film your first UGC sample today, without tagging the brand.

Do I need lots of followers?

text.creator_brand:
Always disclose paid, gifted and affiliate posts. It is required in many countries and it protects the trust your audience gives you.

1. Put #ad or "Paid partnership with [brand]" at the start of the caption.
2. Turn on your platform's paid partnership or branded-content tool.
3. Say it out loud in videos where you can.

Next step: open the disclosure checklist and find the branded-content setting in your app.

text.creator_brand:
Negative comments sting, and they happen to every creator. You decide which ones deserve your energy.

1. Sort it: useful criticism, misunderstanding or abuse.
2. Reply calmly to useful criticism and misunderstandings, or leave them.
3. Hide, block or report abuse without guilt, and add word filters.

Next step: step away for an hour before you reply to anything that upset you.

text.creator_brand:
Feeling tired is a signal to make the plan smaller, not to stop. Rest is part of a sustainable brand.

1. Drop to a rhythm you can keep, even two posts a week.
2. Repurpose an old post instead of creating from scratch.
3. Set a time limit for replies and scrolling each day.

Next step: pick one day off this week and protect it.

followUps: I keep comparing myself to others.

text.creator_brand:
Comparing your start to someone else's middle is unfair to you. Most creators you admire posted for a long time before anyone noticed.

1. Compare yourself only with your own posts from last month.
2. Write three things you have improved since Day 1.
3. Unfollow or mute accounts that make you feel worse rather than inspired.

Next step: write down one post you are proud of and why.
